spans.content: UNICURVSEG: LEARNING CONTEXTUAL PROMPT FOR UNIVERSAL VESSEL-LIKE
CURVILINEAR STRUCTURE SEGMENTATION
Qiuting Hu1†, Li Lin1,2†, Pujin Cheng1,2, Xiaoying Tang1,3,*
1Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology
Shenzhen, China
2Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, The University of Hong Kong,
Hong Kong SAR, China
3Jiaxing Research Institute, Southern University of Science and Technology,
Jiaxing, China
ABSTRACT
Universal model excels at handling multi-task and multi-
modal medical image segmentation, effectively addressing
the variations between different tasks. However, most ex-
isting universal models fail to adequately consider the in-
terrelations between different structures, overlooking their
latent semantic connections. In this paper, we propose a
novel prompt-driven model based on in-context learning that
aims to achieve 3D universal vessel-like curvilinear structure
segmentation (UniCurvSeg) across domains and modalities.
In UniCurvSeg, a learnable task prompt is designed to cap-
ture the correlations across all tasks, integrating a modality
prompt to help the model recognise features from different
modalities and a region prompt to accurately localize target
regions. These prompts are injected into feature maps through
cross-attention, addressing the challenges of data heterogene-
ity and annotation discrepancies. In addition, we incorporate
a dual attention mechanism to learn rich hierarchical repre-
sentations of vessel-like structures. Extensive experimental
results demonstrate that UniCurvSeg outperforms existing
methods on 9 datasets (1662 images) across three modalities
(CT, MRI, MRA).
Index Terms— Universal model, in-context learning,
medical image segmentation, multi-attention
1. INTRODUCTION
Many studies suggest that the geometric and morphological
changes of vessel-like structures (e.g., hepatic vessel, aorta
and brain vessel) in medical image are closely linked to var-
ious diseases [1]. Medical image segmentation plays a cru-
cial role in computer-aided detection and diagnosis, enabling
precise delineation of anatomical structures. In recent years,
deep learning (DL) has achieved remarkable success in med-
ical image segmentation, with single-task models[2] [3] be-
coming the prevailing paradigm. However, due to the high
cost of medical data collection and annotation, single-task
model is often constrained by limited training data. Further-
more, different tasks require specialized networks, resulting
in distributed research efforts.
Several strategies, including multi-head and universal
models, have been proposed to address these challenges.
Multi-head models typically fall into three categories: (1) A
shared encoder with task-specific decoders, exemplified by
Med3D [4], which facilitates feature sharing across tasks. (2)
Task-specific encoders with a shared decoder [5], effectively
handling diverse input modalities by learning and fusing
distinct features at a semantic level. (3) Task-specific en-
coders and decoders connected through shared middle layers
[6], balancing specialized learning with knowledge transfer.
However, these models require strong task relevance and
often lead to structural redundancy due to the need for mul-
tiple specialized components. There is a growing interest in
developing universal models. DoDnet [7] employs one-hot
encoding and a controller to generate dynamic convolutions
for multi-task segmentation. Uniseg [8] introduces a prompt-
driven universal segmentation model. FedLPPA [9] employs
two learnable prompts and n one-hot prompts, integrating
learnable parameters with predefined one-hot encodings to
elicit a more nuanced and efficient response. Hermes [10]
leverages contextual prior learning to effectively integrate
task and modality information. However, these methods pri-
marily focus on segmenting various anatomical structures,
such as organs and tumors, failing to fully harness the seman-
tic consistency shared among similar structures, which limits
their performance across diverse structures. In contrast to
specialized model, universal model can achieve superior per-
formance by learning from the representations of analogous
topologies [11]. In such context, it is desirable to design a
universal framework for structures with similar morphology.

ious diseases [1]. Medical image segmentation plays a cru-
cial role in computer-aided detection and diagnosis, enabling

ical image segmentation, with single-task models[2] [3] be-
coming the prevailing paradigm. However, due to the high

more, different tasks require specialized networks, resulting
in distributed research efforts.
Several strategies, including multi-head and universal
models, have been proposed to address these challenges.
Multi-head models typically fall into three categories: (1) A
shared encoder with task-specific decoders, exemplified by

Task-specific encoders with a shared decoder [5], effectively
handling diverse input modalities by learning and fusing

coders and decoders connected through shared middle layers
[6], balancing specialized learning with knowledge transfer.
However, these models require strong task relevance and

encoding and a controller to generate dynamic convolutions

In this paper, we introduce a novel framework with learn-
able prompts and dual-attention mechanism for universal
vessel-like structures curvilinear segmentation (UniCurvSeg).
In UniCurvSeg, prompts represent the task, modality and tar-
get region, which are fused with feature via a cross-attention
mechanism, and a dual-attention module is introduced for
network to efficiently extract vessel-like structures. The con-
tributions of our work are as follows:
• We propose a universal segmentation paradigm for the
segmentation of vessel-like curvilinear structure, capable
of handling tasks across different anatomical regions and
modalities.
• We introduce a Tri-prompt Fusion (TPF) module for in-
context learning, enabling model to adapt to task, modal-
ity, and region priors for contextual prompt learning.
• A Dual-attention (DA) module is introduced to generate
attention-aware feature representations, effectively utiliz-
ing multi-channel spatial information for feature represen-
tation and normalization, allowing the network to better
distinguish vessel-like structures from the background.
• Results across 9 datasets demonstrate that UniCurvSeg
clearly outperforms other single-task and multi-task mod-
els in the segmentation of vessel-like structures.
2. METHOD
In this section, we first briefly overview our UniCurvSeg
framework, followed by an introduction of the TPF and DA
modules. The TPF module leverages in-context learning,
allowing the model to grasp shared knowledge across tasks,
modalities, and regions, while the DA module capture rich
hierarchical representations of vessel-like structures. The
overview of UniCurvSeg is provided in Fig. 1.
2.1. UniCurvSeg Paradigm Overview
Generally, N segmentation tasks requires designing N unique
architectures, which limits the ability to leverage information
from other tasks and prevents the model from capturing se-
mantic connections between similar structures. To address
this, we propose a universal vessel-like curvilinear structure
segmentation framework that enables a single model to per-
form segmentation across nine common curvilinear structure
datasets spanning three modalities. Given a set of N datasets

3. EXPERIMENTS
3.1. Dataset and Preprecessing
We collect 9 datasets involving 3 regions—thoracic, abdom-
inal, and brain—and 3 imaging modalities: CT, MRI, and
MRA. As shown in Table 1, all images come from public

datasets within the widely used nnU-Net framework. Firstly,

the spacing is resampled to a uniform

Then, image intensities are normalized, followed by further

3.2. Implementation Details
We implement UniCurvSeg using PyTorch on NVIDIA RTX
A6000 GPU, integrating it within the widely adopted nnU-
Net framework. During training, we utilize the SGD opti-
mizer with a learning rate of 0.01, a batch size of 2, and a
default patch size of 64

The model undergoes
training for 1000 epochs, amounting to 450,000 iterations.
3.3. Comparisons with State-of-the-art
We benchmark UniCurvSeg against several representative
segmentation frameworks, covering both commonly used
single-task model like nnU-Net [2], 3D-TransUNet [21] and
U-Mamba [22], and universal model, such as DoDnet [7],
Uniseg [8] and Hermes [10]. For a fair comparison, all
tasks across the single-task models adopt the same number
of epochs, batch size, and patch size as used in our method.
It is worth noting that 3D-TransUNet employs transformer
encoder and transformer encoder, and U-Mamba only use the
U-Mmaba block in the bottleneck.
As shown in Table 2, our method achieves the best perfor-
mance on average Dice score and achieves the highest Dice
score on 8 clinical anatomical structures in 6 datasets. More-
over, UniCurvSeg also present superior performance with an
average margin of 1.49% compared to second-best universal
model, demonstrating its superior performance. Visualization
results for all methods on 4 datasets are provided in Fig. 2.
3.4. Ablation Studies
We conducted a series of intra-component ablations to investi-
gate the efffectiveness of each key component in UniCurvSeg.

It is worth noting that 3D-TransUNet employs transformer
encoder and transformer encoder, and U-Mamba only use the
U-Mmaba block in the bottleneck.
As shown in Table 2, our method achieves the best perfor-
mance on average Dice score and achieves the highest Dice
score on 8 clinical anatomical structures in 6 datasets. More-
over, UniCurvSeg also present superior performance with an
average margin of 1.49% compared to second-best universal
model, demonstrating its superior performance. Visualization
results for all methods on 4 datasets are provided in Fig. 2.

We conducted a series of intra-component ablations to investi-
gate the efffectiveness of each key component in UniCurvSeg.

3.4.1. Ablation studies of TPF
In the ablation of TPF module, we retain the dual-attention
module while systematically ablating the different prompts to
examine the impact of various prompts. Since TP provides
the model with explicit task information and guidance, serv-
ing as the foundation of the universal model, it remains a con-
stant element in this ablation experiment. From Table 3, it is
evident that the addition of either MP or RP leads to a no-
ticeable improvement in performance, and the integration of
both, forming the triple prompt composition, achieves the best
performance outcomes.

3.4.2. Ablation studies of DA
Moreover, we explore the effectiveness of the dual attention
module. Table 4 demonstrates that variants without attention
block yield inferior outcomes. The introduction of either the
spatial attention block or the channel attention block enhances
performance, while the incorporation of both together yields
the best outcomes, underscoring the importance of the atten-
tion module.

4. CONCLUSION
This study propose a novel universal segmentation frame-
work, UniCurvSeg, to address the challenging problem of
multi-task segmentation. A TPF module and a DA module are
introduced to enable in-context learning and effectively ex-
tract vessel-like structures. Extensive experiments conducted
on nine medical imaging datasets across three modalities
successfully demonstrate the superiority of UniCurvSeg.
